name: encryption_extent
description: Measure where, in the bytes of named files, the entropy looks encrypted, and say which bytes were never looked at. It reads explicit files (`files`) or the candidate rows of an encrypted_survey census given by reference (`census`: the path of that census; its last line is a receipt whose `parser` must be `encrypted_survey/3`, and any other value, or a census with no receipt, is refused by name or reported as partial), under a policy the caller declares: `sampling` (the file is cut into windows of `window` bytes; a file of more than `sample_windows` windows gets that many windows spread evenly from its first byte to its last, a smaller one is read whole) or `full` (every byte in order while the read budget and the clock last). For every window it computes the entropy with the same function encrypted_survey uses (a test holds the two sources equal), unrounded, and compares it with `threshold` (default 7.5, this pack's, so that the two tools agree on what is high; the reverse-engineering pack's entropy_map uses 7.2 to find packed regions of executables, which does not keep compressed data apart from encrypted data). A window is high when its unrounded entropy is at or above the threshold; adjacent high windows of a contiguous scan form a run. The answer gives per file: the bytes inspected and the uninspected ranges (the first 16 in the row, every one in the profile file), `high_entropy_fraction`, the runs (the first 16 in the row), a histogram of window entropies in whole bits, and `block_pattern` (observed only when three or more runs of equal length recur at equal spacing in a contiguous scan; it is an observed pattern of windows, it names no family and does not say what the gaps hold; a sampled file is not contiguous and shows none). `high_entropy_fraction` is the share of the INSPECTED bytes that lie in high windows. It is not a percentage of the file that was encrypted and the tool never says so: compressed, packed and random-looking formats are high entropy too (a row says so when the name or the format is one of those), a window that was not read says nothing, and a pattern finer than the window is not located (a window of fewer than about 1000 bytes seldom reaches 7.5 even when its bytes are random; the answer states what a random window reads at the chosen size). It also checks the structure at the head and the end of a file, as booleans only: the magic of the format the caller named or the first extension of the name that names a supported format (pdf, zip and the office and archive formats built on it, png, jpeg, gif, sqlite, gzip, 7z, text), whether the footer is present, and whether the container's directory parses (the zip end record and the first central-directory header, the PDF startxref target, the PNG IHDR chunk, the SQLite page size against the file size, the 7z start-header checksum, UTF-8 decodability for text); it reads up to 4096 bytes at the head and 65,557 at the end, counted in the read budget; a value `null` means the check does not apply to the format. It compares each inspected window byte for byte with the window at the same offset of a plaintext counterpart the caller names for a file (`counterpart`; whether it is authentic is the caller's word, recorded as given and not verified; a counterpart of another size is not compared). It judges a file against a layout only when the caller supplies one (`layout`: rules of the form start or end, offset, length, expected high or not high; each rule is read and reported as consistent, inconsistent, outside the file or not read); the layout is not validated, the findings identify no family, and the tool has no family or actor field. It prints no byte of any file and no value: only counts, offsets, entropies and booleans. The tool never states that a share of a file was encrypted, never says a file is recovered, and never names a family. `status` (also `complete`) is `complete` only when at least one file was named, every named file was opened, every one of its bytes was inspected, no census line was skipped, the census (if any) has a receipt that says complete and no limit was reached; otherwise it is `partial` with `status_basis` and `partial_reasons` (policy `sampling` leaves bytes between the windows, so its answer is partial whenever a file is larger than its windows, and says how many bytes were not inspected; a file that could not be opened, a link, a special file or an invalid path is `not_inspected` with its reason and is counted). An explicit list holds at most 20000 files; a census is streamed row by row with a line limit of 1 MiB (a longer line is counted and skipped), so its size is not bounded except by the clock. Every path is printed through the rule encrypted_survey uses (its manifest states the shape of an identifier, the rates at which it misses and at which it withholds, and the 'another shape is printed' caveat; the code is the same text, held equal by tests): a directory component holding an identifier-shaped token, and the name of a file named like a note, is withheld; the name of any other file is printed as it is, because it is the evidence; the counterpart's path is printed the same way; `paths_withheld` counts the withheld paths. A census row whose path was withheld by the survey has no path to open and is `not_inspected` (name_withheld_in_census). A second check reads every string of the answer and of the files it names on the way out and replaces one that is still identifier-shaped, making a complete answer partial. The profile (`encryption_extent-profile-<digest>.jsonl`, the digest of the parameters, never of a name) holds one JSON line per window (file_id, offset, length, entropy, high, and equal_to_counterpart when compared), per run, per uninspected range and per file, then a receipt; it is written under a temporary name and placed when complete, and a profile or page file already there is never replaced, even by a rerun with other limits: the new one takes the next free name (`-2`, `-3`) and the answer names it, so a rerun with a smaller max_seconds keeps the larger earlier file. Tables longer than `limit` are written whole as JSON Lines and named in pages; the rows shown inline also stop at about 512 KiB. Memory does not grow with the number of windows or files: a full scan of a 64 MiB file at window 64 (1,048,576 windows, the worst case for rows) took 19.1 s at 23 MB resident and wrote 106,687,821 bytes (about 102 bytes per window, so the profile grows with the bytes read: about 1.6 bytes per byte read at window 64 and about 0.025 at window 4096, and only the clock and read_budget_bytes bound it); a 64 MiB window takes about 2.3 s to measure, so a window is not started when the time left is less than 60 ns per byte of it or of the slowest window of 1 MiB or more seen so far. The tool's own clock `max_seconds` (default 780, at most 840, below the manifest's 900) is checked before every window, every census line and every file, and the answer is partial when it runs out; the job's own timeout_seconds is not passed to the tool. `read_budget_bytes` (default 4294967296) counts every byte read: windows, counterpart windows, structure checks and layout rules; when it is spent the rest of a file is uninspected. It reads only regular files, opens them without following a link and without blocking (a named pipe is refused by its fstat, never read), and never writes outside the output directory. A stop signal (SIGTERM, SIGINT, SIGHUP) ends it with one JSON answer (status failed, interrupted, exit code 128 + the signal) after removing the profile and pages it was writing. The handlers are installed when the tool's module code has run as far as its stop block: the start of the interpreter and the compiling of the file come first, and a stop signal in that window (the first moments of the run) can end the tool with no JSON answer at all. SIGKILL cannot be caught: a tool killed that way leaves the hidden temporary files of the profile and the pages in tool-output, and, in a window of microseconds, an empty file at a result name; delete them.

policy.description: Required, declared: `sampling` (at most sample_windows windows of window bytes spread over each file; the rest is listed as uninspected and the answer is partial) or `full` (every byte in order, while the read budget and the clock last)

files.description: The files to measure, at most 20000: a path, or an object {path, format, counterpart, counterpart_authenticated}. `format` is one of pdf, zip, png, jpeg, gif, sqlite, gzip, 7z, text and says which structure to check (default: the first extension of the name that names one). `counterpart` is the path of a plaintext copy of the same size; `counterpart_authenticated` is the caller's word that it is authentic (default false, recorded as given)

census.description: The path of an encrypted_survey census (JSON Lines, one row per entry, a last line `record: receipt` with `parser: encrypted_survey/3`), by reference. Its rows with a status in census_statuses are measured, by the path the census prints; an unknown parser is refused by name, a census without a receipt is read and the answer is partial

census_statuses.description: Which census rows to measure: any of candidate, noncandidate, unmeasured, read_failed (default ["candidate"])

window.description: Bytes per window, 64 to 67108864 (default 4096). A window of fewer than about 1000 bytes seldom reaches 7.5 even when random; the answer says what a random window of this size reads. One window is held in memory

threshold.description: Bits per byte at or above which a window is high, above 0 and at most 8 (default 7.5, this pack's; the reverse-engineering pack's 7.2 finds packed regions of executables and is too low to keep compressed data apart from encrypted data)

sample_windows.description: Under sampling, the number of windows per file, 1 to 4096 (default 64); a file of no more windows than this is read whole

layout.description: Optional, supplied by the caller: {name, validated, source, rules: [{from: start|end, offset, length, expect: high_entropy|not_high_entropy}]}, at most 32 rules, each of at most 67108864 bytes. Each rule is read and reported against its expectation; `validated` is the caller's word and is recorded as given; no family is named

check_structure.description: Check the magic, the footer and the container directory of each file (default true); false skips the head and end reads

limit.description: Rows shown inline in the files table (default 200); every row is counted, and a table with more is written whole as JSON Lines and named in pages.files.all_results. The rows shown inline also stop at about 512 KiB whatever limit says (pages.files.inline_cut_by_size names that cut)

read_budget_bytes.description: The most this run reads in all, windows, counterparts, structure checks and layout rules together (default 4294967296, at least 4096). When it is spent the rest of a file is uninspected and the answer is partial

max_seconds.description: The tool's own time limit in seconds (default 780, at most 840; the manifest's timeout is 900). When it runs out no further window is started, what was measured is written, and the answer is partial
